design_rationale:
WORKLOG - task 0 of financing_plan_desk (Belrose Fine Jewelers, promotional financing).

STEP 0. DIFFICULTY PRE-CHECK AND THE DRAW.
Read first: the three artifact contracts under skills/erl-task-instantiate/references/, then
blueprint.yaml (this difficulty claims category financing and the fourteen financing event types),
products/financing.yaml (six promotional terms, eleven base policies, twenty-one events), db_schema.json
and share_tools.py (verification threshold K=2, so two self-stated details must match).
Counts drawn by code, not chosen:
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/draw_counts.py env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/tasks/financing_plan_desk --tasks 2
  {"task": 0, "key": "fine_jewelry_retailer/financing_plan_desk/0", "prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [6, 5, 5]}
  {"task": 1, "key": "fine_jewelry_retailer/financing_plan_desk/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 4, 4, 6]}
So task 0 is a tree of three problems, two of them prerequisites, and the three computations carry 6, 5
and 5 factors. Assignment made by the author (the multiset is what the gate checks): the lateness charge
takes 6, the returned-payment charge 5, the settlement figure 5.
Occupied before this task: nothing. Claimed by this task: financing_ext_returned_payment_charge,
financing_ext_lateness_charge, financing_ext_settlement_figure, with the tools
book_returned_payment_charge_6a9e81de, book_lateness_charge_0092ea40 and confirm_plan_settlement_d71750ce.
Left for task 1 (which needs four problems): the whole merchandise-return, schedule-rebuild,
service-recovery give-back and hardship-arrangement space - base policies financing_return_credit,
financing_hardship_arrangement and financing_courtesy_waiver, and the events
financing_return_credit_posted, financing_plan_terms_updated, financing_fee_waiver_applied and
financing_hardship_enrolled, none of which this task touches. Task 0 deliberately leaves the
give-back space alone: it only reads an old give-back as history, it never writes one.

WHY THIS MAKES A GOOD TEST.
The caller asks one thing - clear the plan today and close it - and names no number. To answer, the
agent has to notice two debts the records already owe but nobody has booked (a returned payment with no
charge against it, and a due date that no settled payment answers), book them in the right amounts, and
only then work out the settlement figure on the account as it then stands. Getting the number right
means reconciling eighteen ledger entries over sixteen months, fixing which of six promotional terms
applies, reading two other product registers (a trade-in registration and a care coverage record) and a
third (a workshop order), and getting five separate branch decisions right. No step is a matter of
choosing between similar tools: there are three tools and each is named by exactly one policy.

STEP 0 CARDS.
Base-invariant card.
 - Subject financing_returned_payment_fee_assessed -> the only governing base policy is
   financing_evt_returned_payment, whose one applicable gate is the dedup gate
   one_fee_per_returned_payment: "A returned payment fee is charged against a returned payment only when
   no returned payment fee already stands against that same returned payment entry." Authority
   system_record, timing pre_action, correlation key financing_ledger.source_entry_id bound to the call's
   source_entry_id. Satisfied here: the plan's one returned-payment charge, booked 2026-02-20, names
   the return of 2026-02-18 as its source entry; the only other entry with a source entry is the
   give-back of 2026-03-20, which answers the lateness charge of 2026-03-05. The return of 2026-09-02
   carries no charge, and the charge policy's own rule fixes it as the object: "The returned payment
   the charge answers is the most recently presented payment the bank has sent back unpaid on the
   plan." Cycle 2026-09 carries no returned-payment charge, inside the term's ceiling of two.
 - Subject financing_late_fee_assessed -> financing_evt_late_fee, two applicable gates.
   grace_period_elapsed is a time gate: anchor event "the payment due date printed on the statement for
   that billing cycle", anchor source financing_ledger.payment_due_date, relation not_before, duration
   variants.grace_period_days (five days on this term), unit calendar days, day of the due date counting
   as day zero, boundary exclusive. Positive case: due 2026-08-15 plus five days gives 2026-08-20; the
   handling date 2026-09-17 is twenty-eight days past that boundary, so the charge is due. Negative case:
   on 2026-08-20 itself the boundary is only equalled and, the boundary being exclusive, the payment is
   not yet late - the desk waits. The second gate, plan_billing_or_delinquent, allows active or past due;
   the plan stands past due.
 - Subject financing_plan_closed_paid and financing_payment_posted -> financing_closure_and_payoff and
   financing_evt_payment_allocation. quote_still_valid is a time gate: anchor "the date the payoff quote
   was issued to the customer", source financing_intake.created_at, relation not_after, duration
   variants.payoff_quote_validity_days (fourteen on this term), counted with the day of issue as day
   zero, boundary inclusive. The quote was taken 2026-09-11; the handling date is its sixth day, inside
   the window; on 2026-09-25 it would still stand and on 2026-09-26 it would not. plan_open_for_payment
   allows approved, active, past due or in hardship; the plan stands past due. The other gate of
   financing_closure_and_payoff, approved_before_billing, applies only to financing_plan_activated and is
   not a subject of this task, so it is not inherited here.
 - No eligibility of any governing policy is weakened. Two base handling clauses are superseded, each
   declared clause by clause in the policy's own overwrite block: the payoff-figure sentence of
   financing_closure_and_payoff, and the first-versus-repeat sentence of financing_evt_late_fee, and the
   returned-payment-fee sentence of financing_evt_returned_payment. Every other base sentence, parameter
   value and gate stays in force and stays base-homed.
Business-object card.
 The narrowest object of each write. The returned-payment charge attaches to one ledger entry, the
 payment posted 2026-09-02 whose outcome is returned_nsf, and the tool writes that entry's id into the
 new row's source entry, so it can never be read as answering the other return of 2026-02-18 - which
 was charged at the time, on 2026-02-20, and is excluded by the base dedup sentence. The
 lateness charge attaches to one payment due date, 2026-08-15, printed on the statement closed
 2026-07-21, and the tool writes that date onto the new row; the other unanswered due date in the file,
 2026-02-15, was already answered by the lateness charge of 2026-03-05, and the most recent due date,
 2026-09-15, is only two days old and still inside the term's grace. The settlement attaches to the one
 promotional financing plan this customer holds. Rows included in the standing-charge sum: every
 lateness charge, returned-payment charge and give-back on this plan; rows excluded: purchases,
 statements and payments, which are not priced charges. The give-back of 2026-03-20 is correlated to the
 lateness charge of 2026-03-05 by its source entry and settles that charge alone.
Problem-tree card.
 Root: financing_ext_settlement_figure (target confirm_plan_settlement_d71750ce, owner user).
 Prerequisites: financing_ext_returned_payment_charge (book_returned_payment_charge_6a9e81de, owner
 agent) and financing_ext_lateness_charge (book_lateness_charge_0092ea40, owner agent). Shape: a fan-out
 of two parallel edges from the root. Two prerequisite problems, exactly the draw; at least
 max(2-1,1) = 1 value_input edge is required and both edges are value_input.
 Edge 1 - from financing_ext_settlement_figure to financing_ext_returned_payment_charge, kind
   value_input, gate standing_charges, form state. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the root's own
   rule: "The settlement figure is worked out only after every payment the bank has sent back unpaid on
   the plan carries the returned-payment charge owed against it in the billing history." Four-point test:
   (1) "only after" joins the root's own result to what it waits on; (2) the XX side is a record-visible
   state - a returned payment entry carrying a charge against it, in the words the ledger and the finder
   use; (3) it names no tool, no policy id, no code token; (4) its strength is a hard requirement and its
   scope is exactly "every payment the bank has sent back unpaid on the plan", the same set as the edge's
   condition. Exactly one write in this difficulty brings that state about: only
   financing_ext_returned_payment_charge books an entry whose source entry is a returned payment, which
   its own rule states in its own terms ("charged against the returned payment entry itself"). Derivation:
   the sentence says charges must stand against every returned payment; the records show the payment of
   2026-09-02 returned and no entry pointing back at it; the returned-payment charge policy is the one
   rule whose write books such an entry; therefore that write, and no other, is the resolving action.
   Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: initial_state.financing_ledger.<R1>.payment_outcome =
   returned_nsf; the plan's one returned-payment charge, initial_state.financing_ledger.<RPF2>, names
   the 2026-02-18 return as its source_entry_id; and the only other entry with a source entry,
   initial_state.financing_ledger.<GB1>, points at the lateness charge of 2026-03-05. So exactly one
   returned payment on the plan - the 2026-09-02 one - stands uncharged.
 Edge 2 - from financing_ext_settlement_figure to financing_ext_lateness_charge, kind value_input, gate
   standing_charges, form state. Prerequisite sentence, verbatim from the root's own rule: "The
   settlement figure is worked out only after every missed payment due date printed on the plan's
   statements carries the lateness charge due against it in the billing history." Same four-point test:
   ordering connective "only after"; a record-visible state (a due date on a statement carrying a
   lateness charge entry); no tool, id or code token; the scope is exactly the missed due dates printed
   on the plan's statements. Exactly one write brings it about: only financing_ext_lateness_charge books
   a lateness charge carrying a due date. Seed evidence that it is false at the opening: the statement
   row <ST2> prints payment_due_date 2026-08-15; the only payment presented against it, <R1>, carries
   payment_outcome returned_nsf; and the only lateness charge in the file, <LF1>, carries
   payment_due_date 2026-02-15.
 Topological order: returned-payment charge, lateness charge, settlement. Parallel edges commute (see
 prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness, where the actual reasoning and the run are recorded).
 Deletion sensitivity, from the Step 5 run: skip the returned-payment charge and the settlement falls
 from 1,181.95 to 1,160.95; skip the lateness charge and it falls to 1,148.65. Both edges bear weight.
 No problem of the tree waits on anything outside the conversation: both charges are book entries the
 desk makes on the spot, and the settlement is money the customer moves on the spot. Nothing here is a
 diagnosis, a delivery, a clearing cycle or a future date.

STEP 1. THE POLICIES.
financing_ext_returned_payment_charge (state_due; the money is owed at month-end whether or not anyone
rings). Baseline, which is all the computation document will say: the base charge is the term's returned
payment fee, three allowances are each worked out on their own and taken off it once, never one off
another, and the result is rounded to the cent and floored at nothing. Five factors: the base-charge band
(parameter), the return-history reading (method, a window convention), the presentation-channel allowance
(parameter), the care-coverage allowance (parameter, cross-difficulty on protection) and the
plan-standing allowance (parameter). Two parameter factors are required and there are four; one method
factor is required and there is one.
financing_ext_lateness_charge (state_due). Baseline: the base charge is the term's first-lateness fee,
no uplift, no allowance, the two added first, the allowance taken off that sum, rounded at the end only.
Six factors: the lateness-history window (method), the counted lateness history (method), the base-charge
band (parameter), the clock anchor (method), the delinquency uplift band (parameter) and the workshop
relationship allowance (parameter, cross-difficulty on service).
financing_ext_settlement_figure (on_request; it is a quote-like figure that arises only because the
customer asks to settle). Baseline: balance, plus interest over the final part of the cycle at the term's
promotional rate from the closing date of the most recent statement on a 365-day year, plus the priced
charges standing unanswered read over the term's repeat window, added, rounded and floored at nothing.
Five factors: the settlement rate band (parameter), the final-period anchor (method), the repricing
review window (method), the standing-charge reading (method) and the upgrade-credit offset (parameter,
cross-difficulty on tradein, and multi-source).
Multi-source floor: the task needs one and carries several - the return base-charge band, the care
coverage allowance, the lateness clock anchor, the workshop relationship allowance and the upgrade-credit
offset each combine two conditions over distinct evidence on every tier beyond the fall-through.
Cross-difficulty floor: the task needs one and carries three, reading three different difficulties'
registers - protection (coverage standing, premium schedule parameter, premium ledger), service (work
order standing and rework count) and tradein (registration standing, remaining credit, and the
programme's part-spending parameter). Every one of them reads a value, not a bare existence.
Forward and reverse sweep rule <-> compute_basis <-> compute: every binding that reads the world,
aggregates, branches, caps or rounds carries a verbatim rule quotation (twelve quotations on the
settlement figure, thirteen on the lateness charge, eleven on the returned-payment charge). Swept back
the other way, every load-bearing sentence of each rule is claimed by a binding: the three window
sentences by review_window_months, charge_window_months, returns_window_months and repeat_window_months;
the three ladder sentences of each policy by their ladder bindings; the ordering and rounding sentences
by result; the acting-base and combination semantics are pinned in prose ("each of them is worked out on
its own and taken off the base charge once, so that they are never applied one to the result of
another"; "The base charge and the delinquency uplift are added first, the relationship allowance is
taken off that sum, the figure is rounded to the cent at the end only"). No sentence is left unclaimed
and no filter in an expression is missing from its quotation.

STEP 2. THE TOOLS.
Capability contract cards, written before the code.
 book_returned_payment_charge_6a9e81de - owner agent, rw write. Target object: one promotional financing
 plan's billing history. Atomic action: create one ledger entry of the returned-payment-charge family,
 positive, carrying the returned payment as its source entry, posted and cycled on today's date, coded
 returned_payment and allocated to fees. Observable: the charge appears on the plan's history and on the
 next statement. Receipt: one sentence naming the new entry reference, the plan reference and the amount.
 book_lateness_charge_0092ea40 - owner agent, rw write. One ledger entry of the lateness family, positive,
 carrying the missed due date and the lateness code given, posted and cycled on today's date, allocated
 to fees. Receipt: one sentence naming the new entry reference, the plan, the due date and the amount.
 confirm_plan_settlement_d71750ce - owner user, rw write, because paying a plan out disposes of the
 customer's own money and the blueprint reserves that to her. One settled payment entry credited
 negative through the finance desk, plus the plan record set to paid off with today as the closed date
 and the last payment date and the balance emptied. Receipt: one sentence naming the settled payment
 entry and the closed plan.
None of the three reads anything, tests anything or returns a policy refusal; each is a mint-an-id and
call-ctx.create (and, for the settlement, ctx.update) body with the arguments exactly as given. Billing
cycle and posting date are taken from the clock inside the tool rather than offered to the agent, because
they need no judgement. Gate run after writing them:
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_task_tools.py env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/tasks/financing_plan_desk
  -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK

STEP 3. THE WORLD, AND WHY EACH CLASS OF ROW IS THERE.
One customer, one promotional financing plan on the 24-Month Equal Payment Plan, eighteen ledger
entries, one finance-desk request, and one holding in each of three other difficulties.
 - The plan (past due, billing since 2025-04-30, balance 1,842.60, scheduled payment 133.44, automatic
   payment off, no hardship arrangement). Its term fixes every tier parameter read. Its past-due standing
   is what puts the world off the fall-through tier of four separate factors; make it active and the
   repricing review window, the standing-charge reading, the lateness-history window and the lateness
   clock anchor all fall back to their baselines.
 - Nine settled payments, four of them older than six months and five inside six months. Remove the four
   old ones and the missed cycles over the twelve-month review fall from three to seven - still past the
   trigger - but remove instead any of the five recent ones and the six-month baseline reading of the
   review window stops differing from the twelve-month one, which is exactly what makes the
   repricing-review-window factor bear weight. Nine against twelve cycles is three missed; five against
   six cycles is one missed, below the term's trigger of two.
 - Two returned payments and one returned-payment charge. The return posted 2026-09-02 is the object
   of the first prerequisite and the anchor of the lateness clock; the return posted 2026-02-18 is the
   near-miss of the return-history reading: at six whole calendar months from the handling date it sits
   just outside the term's six-month repeat window and just inside the twelve-month past-due reading,
   so a careless reader who uses the ordinary window counts one return and prices the charge at 32.00
   instead of 40.00. The charge of 32.00 booked 2026-02-20 against that February return is what makes
   the first prerequisite single-valued: it names the February return as its source entry, so the
   base dedup sentence forbids a second charge on it and the only return owed a charge is the
   September one. Delete that row and the universal prerequisite sentence would demand two charges.
   The February charge also sits at six whole months, so it enters the settlement's all-since-billing
   charge reading and not the six-month baseline reading.
 - One lateness charge of 35.00 posted 2026-03-05 and one courtesy give-back of -35.00 posted 2026-03-20.
   These are the near-miss pair of the lateness policy: the charge sits at exactly six whole months (just
   outside the ordinary window, just inside the doubled one) while its give-back sits at five (inside
   both), so both the window factor and the counted-history factor turn on them, and the standing-charge
   reading of the settlement figure differs by 35.00 depending on which stretch is read. Delete either row
   and two factors of the lateness charge and one of the settlement figure stop biting.
 - Three statements, closing on the plan's statement day of the twenty-first and printing a due date
   twenty-five days later. The one closed 2026-07-21 prints 2026-08-15, the due date the lateness charge
   answers; the one closed 2026-08-21 prints 2026-09-15, which is the anchor the settlement's final-period
   factor uses and which is itself still inside grace, so it must not be charged. Remove the last
   statement and the final-period anchor has nothing to read.
 - The purchase entry of 3,200.00 ties the plan to receipt BR-2025-118406 and item RING-40218 and matches
   the plan's financed amount.
 - The finance-desk request of 2026-09-11 is the payoff quote the settlement is honoured against; delete
   it and the time gate on the settlement has no authoritative anchor.
 - Trade-in registration TU-418206 (Bridal Upgrade Guarantee, credit issued, 750.00 still available). The
   programme's part-spending parameter is what puts the customer on the first tier of the upgrade-credit
   factor rather than the second. Delete the row and the settlement rises by 750.00.
 - Care coverage on the Belrose Lifetime Care Plan, in force, premium collected monthly, with premiums
   taken 2026-07-01 and 2026-08-01. Delete either premium row and the coverage allowance falls to the
   single-payment tier or to nothing.
 - Work order WO-772140, in the workshop, rework count one. Delete it and the lateness charge rises by
   20.00.
Automatic clauses checked row by row before seeding: nothing in the file lights an obligation this task
set cannot discharge. The plan is past due but far short of the term's ninety-day reinstatement limit and
its one-hundred-and-eighty-day write-off threshold, so neither reinstatement nor charge-off is owed. The
term is an equal-payment term, so it holds back no interest and nothing about deferred interest can
arise; accrued_promo_interest is 0.00 accordingly. The promotional term does not end until 2027-04-30, so
no expiry notice or term-close billing is due. The care coverage's next inspection falls 2026-10-11, after
the handling date. The trade-in credit expires 2028-05-20. No cache trap was designed here: the plan's
balance field is the truth and the diagnostic that reports it differing from the ledger sum is only
noting that the seeded history is a window on a longer life, not a discrepancy the task tests.
Prerequisites actively falsified: see the problem-tree card and prerequisite_closure - the returned
payment carries no charge, and the missed due date carries none either. Both are false as a matter of
seeded fact, and both flip true the moment the corresponding write lands.

STEP 4. THE PERSONA.
Marguerite is written as a clipped, unhurried professional who asks short questions. She volunteers only
three things: the goal (clear the plan today, in one payment, closed), the circumstance behind it (a
mortgage file being looked at again), and one natural aside (her ring is at the workshop again). Every
one of those is independently true of the opening world - the plan is open and past due, and work order
WO-772140 stands in the workshop with a rework against it. She gives her mobile number and postal code
only as they are asked for, her date of birth and email if more is needed, and she declines to read a
card number aloud, saying instead she will pay from the account on file; that is the must-ask question
that never enters gold, and it has a definite answer. She does not know the balance and says she would
rather it were read off the account than guessed at, which is the natural reason no figure of hers can
compete with the record. She never mentions a fee, a bounced payment, a give-back or anything that has
to be put right first; her only contribution on that head is a passive one - if the agent says the
account has to be brought up to date first, she says that is fine and waits. She asks to run the payment
herself, which is what hands the customer's own tool over. Her arc closes exactly where the evaluation
closes: she reacts to the confirmation of the settlement and rings off, asking for nothing further - no
letter, no statement, no address.

STEP 5. VERIFICATION, ACTUALLY RUN.
The recomputation was run before any gold was filled in, with the policies and the seed on disk, using
the gate's own evaluator so that the numbers are the ones the gate will recompute. The script is
reproduced by the gate itself; the run and its output were:
  .venv/bin/python skills/erl-task-instantiate/scripts/check_compute.py env/env_0001_fine_jewelry_retailer/tasks/financing_plan_desk --task 0
  task comps fact xfac hist brch step match
  0.json   3   16    3   22   53   15  True
  COMPUTE OK
Per-problem, on each problem's own handling-time world:
  returned-payment charge, on the opening world: result 21.00; factor baselines 13.00, 13.00, 27.00,
    29.00, 26.00; every-factor baseline 32.00.
  lateness charge, on the opening world: result 33.30; factor baselines 25.50, 25.50, 25.50, 25.10,
    21.00, 53.30; every-factor baseline 35.00.
  settlement figure, on the world after both charges have landed: result 1,181.95; factor baselines
    1,179.91, 1,220.12, 1,179.91, 1,114.95, 1,931.95; every-factor baseline 1,875.52.
Every factor moves its result, so none is decoration, and every all-baseline figure differs from gold, so
an agent who finds only the computation document computes a definite wrong number. The root was evaluated
on the post-prerequisite world, never on the opening one: on the opening world its standing charges would
be 32.00 and the figure 1,127.65, which is not gold.
Prerequisite sensitivity, run by skipping one write at a time and replaying the rest: skipping the
returned-payment charge gives 1,160.95 (standing charges 65.30); skipping the lateness charge gives
1,148.65 (standing charges 53.00). Both edges therefore bear weight, which is also what the gate's own
value_input test asserts.
Order test: both orders of the two parallel prerequisites were run and give the same two amounts and the
same terminal DB, because neither policy's compute reads the family of entry the other writes.
Whole-input floors: forcing every cross-category read off changes all three results; zeroing the history
aggregates changes all three.

STEP 6. EVALUATION AND CLOSURE.
Read nodes: locate, verify, then the plan, the whole ledger, the finance-desk request, the care
coverage and its premiums, the work order and the trade-in registration - nine reads, none duplicated,
each feeding a named factor or gate. The reads are also the agent's only path to discovering the two
prerequisites: the ledger read is what shows a returned payment with nothing against it and a due date
with no settled payment answering it, and the necessity on that node quotes both prerequisite sentences'
subject matter.
Write nodes in topological order: unlock and call the returned-payment charge (step 10), unlock and call
the lateness charge (step 12), unlock and hand over the settlement, which the customer runs (step 14).
Closure: policy -> target tool -> computation step/arg -> gold call -> terminal state holds for all three;
set(computations.policy_id) equals charter_scope.extended_policies equals the tree; required_documents
repeats that list verbatim and in order; charter_scope.task_tools is the three tools in first-call order.
Negative space proved rather than omitted: the due date of 2026-09-15 printed on the most recent statement
is only two days old at the handling date and the term's grace is five days, so the grace boundary is not
yet passed and no second lateness charge may be booked; the return of 2026-02-18 already carries the
returned-payment charge of 2026-02-20, which names it as its source entry, so the base dedup sentence
forbids a second charge on it and the charge policy's object sentence points at the 2026-09-02 return
alone; the term's per-cycle ceiling of two returned-payment charges is not reached in cycle 2026-09; and no
give-back is due on anything, because the only charge that could be given back was already given back in
March.
Reachability, turn by turn: she states the goal and the timing in her first breath; she gives the mobile
number and the postal code when asked, which is exactly the two the verification tool needs; the plan,
the history, the request record and the three outside registers are all reachable by the share finders;
the agent explains that the account has to be brought up to date, she agrees; the two charges are booked
synchronously; the agent hands her the settlement step, she runs it, and its real return - the entry
reference and the closed plan - enters the shared transcript; she reacts to that and closes. Everything
happens under the one frozen time of 2026-09-17 10:20:00 EDT; nothing waits on a clearing cycle, a
delivery, a review or a future date.

STEP 7. GATES RUN FOR THIS TASK, AND THE BLIND RE-DERIVATION.
  check_extended --task 0     -> EXTENDED OK
  check_task_tools            -> TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK
  replay_tasks --task 0       -> REPLAY OK (15 actions, deterministic, non-vacuous, 0 errors, closure 26 of 26)
  check_solvability --task 0  -> SOLVABILITY OK (3 calls, 5 base gates, 19 seed rows)
  check_compute --task 0      -> COMPUTE OK
  check_grounding --task 0    -> GROUNDING OK (2 identity attributes used, 3 answers, 3 writes, 8 conditional markers)
  check_cross_fire --task 0   -> SCOPE OK
  check_cache_diff --task 0   -> CACHE-DIFF INFO (no cache trap designed here)
Revision recorded: the first run of check_solvability failed on required_user_inputs[3], whose cited
snippet began with a lower-case "she" while the persona sentence begins with "She". Root cause: the
snippet was typed rather than lifted. Change: the citation was corrected to the verbatim sentence. Re-run:
SOLVABILITY OK. No downstream asset referenced that snippet, so nothing else needed propagating.
Revision 2 (rework round 2, from the source-layer audit under audits/policy_task/financing_plan_desk/,
items T0-1 and F-2, plus O-2). Symptom: the audit demonstrated a second defensible terminal state - a
returned-payment charge of 21.00 on the 2026-02-18 return and a settlement of 1,170.95 - because the
seed carried two returned payments and neither carried a charge, while the settlement policy's
prerequisite sentence is universal over every returned payment and the charge policy did not say
which return it prices. Root cause: a world defect (the February return had never been charged, which
the file could not explain) compounded by a false assertion in the tracing and in this dossier that
the February return "already sits outside any charge owed". Change, inside this write domain only and
with base untouched: (1) the seed now carries the returned-payment charge of 32.00 booked 2026-02-20
against the February return, naming it as its source entry, so the base dedup sentence excludes a
second charge on it and exactly one return stands uncharged; (2) the charge policy's rule, baseline
and basis gained the object sentence "The returned payment the charge answers is the most recently
presented payment the bank has sent back unpaid on the plan", which is what its compute already read,

user_scenario:
Marguerite Ashford-Vance is forty-seven, an architect who has lived in the same Upper East Side apartment for eleven years and is now selling it. She is precise, a little clipped, and used to reading contracts, so she asks short questions and waits for the answer rather than filling the silence. What she wants is simple and she says it in the first breath: she has a Belrose financing plan running on the engagement ring her husband bought at the Madison Avenue store, and she wants to clear the whole thing today, in one payment, and have the plan closed. The mortgage people will look at her file again at the end of the month and she wants nothing open on it by then. She telephoned the finance desk a week ago and asked what it would take to clear the plan; she was told a figure would be worked out for her, and that is what she is ringing back about. She is quite clear that she is not asking for an estimate to think about: she wants it settled while she is on the telephone.

She does not know what is owed. The last paper statement is in a drawer somewhere and she has not opened it, and when the agent asks her for a figure she says plainly that she would rather they read it off the account than have her guess at it. She is happy for the agent to go through the account and put right anything on it that needs putting right before the figure is fixed; she says so in as many words if the agent asks for that leave. The one thing she wants to do herself is hand over the money, because it is her money and she likes to be the one who presses the button; so when the agent offers to take the payment for her she declines pleasantly and asks to be given the step to do herself.

She gives her details only as they are asked for, one at a time. The mobile number she gives is 2125553114. The postal code on her billing address is 10021. If the agent needs more, her date of birth is 1979-04-22 and the email on the account is m.ashfordvance@northstarmail.com. She will not read out a card number over the telephone and says so if asked; she will pay from the current account the desk already has on file, and she confirms that she has the account to hand.

In passing, while she waits, she mentions that her ring is at the workshop again — it went in at the end of August for the second time and she is still waiting for it back — and asks only whether that has any bearing on the plan. Whatever she is told about it, she does not press the point. If the agent tells her that the account has to be brought up to date before the figure can be fixed, she says that is fine, she would rather it were right than cheap, and she waits. If the agent reads a figure to her, she does not argue with it and does not offer a figure of her own; she says she will take their word for what the account shows. Once the agent hands her the step to settle the plan, she runs it herself and reads back the confirmation it gives her. When she hears that the plan is closed and settled, she thanks them, says that is one thing off the list, and rings off. She asks for nothing else.

Basis: the tool's schema says, verbatim, 'Id class - the reference number of the billing entry that records the payment the bank returned unpaid; read from the plan's billing history lookup, where returned payments carry the returned outcome.' Uniqueness: of the entries returned at step 3 exactly two carry a returned outcome, the one posted 2026-02-18 and the one posted 2026-09-02; the base rule quoted in the charge policy charges the fee 'against the returned payment itself', and the charge policy's own rule fixes the object: 'The returned payment the charge answers is the most recently presented payment the bank has sent back unpaid on the plan.' The 2026-02-18 return already carries the returned-payment charge of 32.00 booked 2026-02-20, which names it as its source entry, so the base dedup sentence forbids a second charge on it; the 2026-09-02 return is the most recently presented and carries none. argument_uniqueness_tracing.charge_amount: 21.00 USD. The base charge is the term's returned payment fee for the 24-Month Equal Payment Plan, 32.00, raised by the desk's repeat-return share of 25 per cent, because the return history read over the twelve whole calendar months ending on 2026-09-17 (the stretch the past-due standing selects) carries two returns, the entries posted 2026-02-18 and 2026-09-02, and the plan stands past due: 32.00 x 1.25 = 40.00.
